Iran International liveblog (21-23 Nov 2026)

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is scheduled to meet Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani in Washington on Monday, the US State Department said in a statement Sunday.

Iran will not tolerate the US naval blockade and will use all available means to counter it, the Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Monday.

President Donald Trump told Fox News on Sunday that he was inclined to resume strikes on Iran after the new year if no deal was reached, and said Iranian ships testing the US naval blockade would "all be at the bottom of the sea like the rest of the navy."

US Central Command is at maximum readiness and is pushing for a military strike on Iran alongside Israel, i24NEWS reported Sunday, citing Israeli security officials.

The United States has decided for now to postpone any potential military strike on Iran by at least a week, despite pressure from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for a joint offensive, Israeli news outlet Ynet reported Sunday, citing US administration officials.

Iraq closed the Shalamcheh border crossing with Iran until further notice because of disruptions to customs systems, Iran’s semi-official Mehr News Agency reported on Monday.

The United States and Europe cannot bring down Iran unless Iranians do it themselves, the country’s president said on Monday.

“The United States and Europe cannot topple us unless we topple ourselves,” Masoud Pezeshkian said.

He called for compromise, cooperation and treating others with kindness, stressing the need to avoid hostility, sarcasm and labeling one another.

He also said following “God’s and the Imam’s orders” would solve the country’s problems and help it overcome its current situation.

100%Nov 23, 2026, 10:42 GMT+0Video: Man rides donkey in Iran over fuel shortages and rising car costsNov 23, 2026, 10:32 GMT+0Tehran daily says all Europe is within range of Iranian missilesIran’s ballistic missiles could reach around 5,000 kilometers, putting Europe within their range, Tehran municipality’s Hamshahri newspaper said on Monday.

In a graphic headlined “All of Europe within Iran’s reach,” the newspaper said an order for a response without geographical limits could signal a shift in Iran’s deterrence strategy.

It said a possible expansion of Iran’s missile range beyond 2,000 kilometers had raised concern among Western countries.

Hamshahri also said Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei’s guidance to military commanders had drawn greater international attention to Iran’s missile program and its potential range.

100%Nov 23, 2026, 10:10 GMT+0IRGC adviser says airstrikes are Washington’s only military optionA senior Revolutionary Guards adviser said on Monday that the United States cannot launch a ground attack on Iran, and a naval assault would carry heavy risks and costs.

Mohammadreza Naghdi said airstrikes were Washington’s only military option, but any attack on Iran’s vital infrastructure would prompt retaliation.

He made the remarks at a ceremony in Hormozgan Province, according to the state-run IRNA news agency.

Naghdi said US politicians hoped economic pressure and sanctions would discourage Iranians, deepen internal divisions and weaken the resolve of Iran’s officials and armed forces.

He added that officials and military personnel would not retreat under pressure.

Iran’s Intelligence Ministry said on Monday it had arrested 27 people and dismantled “four armed cells” in West Azarbaijan Province in northwest Iran.

The ministry accused the detainees of moving Starlink equipment and weapons from border areas to bring into Iranian cities.

The ministry also accused them of preparing attacks and unrest, and alleged they were acting as part of a US-Israeli plan.

Iran has increased its missile production capacity and improved its drone capabilities, including their range, operational power and reconnaissance, a deputy commander of the Revolutionary Guards said on Monday.

Mostafa Izadi also cited progress in air defense and said enemy aircraft were being targeted continuously.

“We will deliver a strong and effective response to every level and type of threat, without geographical limits,” he said.

100%Nov 23, 2026, 08:57 GMT+0Iran summons Qatari envoy over German-Qatari condemnation of Iranian attacksIran summoned Qatar’s chargé d’affaires to protest a joint German-Qatari statement condemning Iranian attacks on countries in the region, Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Monday.

Esmaeil Baghaei called the statement surprising and regrettable, saying Qatar’s position had been unexpected.

He said Tehran rejected the allegations and had delivered its protest to the chargé d’affaires in the absence of Qatar’s ambassador.

Commenting on Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani’s visit to Washington, Baghaei said ending fighting on all fronts was an integral part of any agreement.

He described the demand as a sign of Iran’s responsibility for regional security and stability.

Responding to remarks by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who said Iran’s rulers were “wounded cornered animals,” Baghaei said: “The Islamic Republic has been wounded, but these wounds have made the lion’s claws and teeth more resilient.”

100%Nov 23, 2026, 08:21 GMT+0Iran says it will use all means to counter US naval blockadeIran will not tolerate the US naval blockade and will use all available means to counter it, the Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Monday.

Esmaeil Baghaei called the blockade an act of “military aggression” and said Iran considered itself entitled under the UN Charter to take political, economic and military measures against it, at a time and in a manner decided by its authorities.

Baghaei also said no decision to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty had been communicated to the ministry. Iran would honor its obligations for as long as it remained a member, he said.

On the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP), Baghaei said Iran distrusted third parties and was monitoring developments. He said Tehran supported expanding economic ties in the South Caucasus but opposed changes to the region’s geopolitics.

100%Nov 23, 2026, 08:10 GMT+0Iran lawmaker says missile range has reached 4,500 km, putting Europe in reachA member of the Iranian parliament’s national security committee said on Monday that the country’s missiles now have a range of 4,500 kilometers and can reach Europe.

Ahmad Bakhshaesh Ardestani said Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei had called for greater accuracy in missiles.

“Our missile range has increased from 2,000 kilometers to 4,500 kilometers, and our young leader has said to make the missiles precise and capable of pinpoint strikes. That means we have Europe in our grasp,” the MP said.

He also criticized Qatar, saying it could no longer serve as an effective mediator because it had condemned Iran while seeking to mediate.
